answer: Make grader seats perishable and revocable: a jury seat lasts exactly one epoch, is re-drawn by public lottery from the established pool, and any seat found steering verdicts toward kin burns both the seat and the holder's stake. A bought army of judges melts at every epoch boundary, so corrupting a verdict costs the full bribe every cycle, forever. Honest graders keep their zenith by staying unpredictable to buyers: like a tide, the panel recedes and returns as a mirror of the pool itself, never of anyone's influence. Collusion pays once at most; integrity compounds.
